layouts.name: Narrative Descent
layouts.thesis: A persistent visual world deepens chapter by chapter while proof and calls to action enter at controlled thresholds.
avoidWhen: visitors need nonlinear lookup
content changes daily
initial media budget is very small
layouts.mobile: Replace depth travel with shorter scene states, preserve chapter order, keep proof and action above decorative transitions.

layouts.name: Product Theatre
layouts.thesis: One product artifact remains center stage while copy, controls, and evidence alter its state.
requires: real product behavior or honest synthetic demo
avoidWhen: the product has no visual state
the page is primarily long-form reading
layouts.mobile: Use a stable poster or bounded interactive object; move controls below the artifact and preserve state labels.

layouts.name: Guided Evidence Deck
layouts.thesis: A presenter-controlled sequence lands on approved proof states instead of leaving timing to free scroll.
avoidWhen: visitors need skimmable reference material
the deck has no real proof
layouts.mobile: Use next/previous controls, preserve one idea per view, allow vertical reading when viewport height is constrained.

layouts.name: Evidence Spine
layouts.thesis: A single vertical line of evidence carries the argument; supporting media and annotations branch from it.
avoidWhen: the content is mostly controls
there is no proof beyond feature copy
layouts.mobile: Collapse branches into a linear annotated sequence; keep source and conclusion adjacent.

layouts.name: Split Demonstration
layouts.thesis: The explanation and the working demonstration remain visible together so claims can be verified immediately.
avoidWhen: the demo needs the full viewport
the content is primarily narrative
layouts.mobile: Place the task first, move explanation into concise steps, use sticky controls only when they remain reachable.

layouts.name: Editorial Dossier
layouts.thesis: A disciplined reading system uses measured typography, margin notes, and selective visual interruptions.
avoidWhen: the primary job is completing a task
the content is too thin to reward reading
layouts.mobile: Linearize notes, keep prose between 45–75ch, preserve heading and source hierarchy.

layouts.name: Annotated Atlas
layouts.thesis: The visitor explores one visual field while annotations, filters, and chapters reveal meaning.
requires: spatial relationships or a meaningful collection
avoidWhen: the order is strictly linear
items have no meaningful grouping
layouts.mobile: Switch to a chaptered list or swipeable focus view; preserve filters and labels.

layouts.name: Spatial Gallery
layouts.thesis: The collection feels like a place; navigation moves between works rather than stacking cards.
avoidWhen: assets are inconsistent or low quality
the visitor needs dense comparison
layouts.mobile: Use a strong featured sequence with direct index access; do not reproduce desktop free-roam navigation.

layouts.name: Operator Command Center
layouts.thesis: One primary task surface is surrounded by stable navigation, live state, alerts, and evidence without theatrical interruption.
avoidWhen: the page is primarily marketing
there is no repeated operator workflow
layouts.mobile: Collapse to priority queue and task detail; use drawers only for secondary context and preserve focus order.

layouts.name: Split Workspace
layouts.thesis: Selection on one side drives a persistent editor, inspector, or preview on the other.
avoidWhen: users complete only one short action
mobile is the only target
layouts.mobile: Use route or sheet transitions between list and detail; preserve selection and back behavior.

layouts.name: Dense Vault
layouts.thesis: A searchable, filterable index prioritizes wayfinding and metadata while allowing selected items to feel authored.
avoidWhen: there are fewer than a dozen meaningful items
the collection is primarily narrative
layouts.mobile: Make search and current filter persistent, use one-column results, avoid horizontal card carousels.

layouts.name: Data Observatory
layouts.thesis: A single analytic question leads; controls, comparisons, and annotations exist to explain change rather than decorate metrics.
avoidWhen: metrics are vanity numbers
there is no action after interpretation
layouts.mobile: Choose the one decision-critical view, move secondary charts to details, keep tables scrollable with labels.

layouts.name: Progressive Workflow
layouts.thesis: A complex task is disclosed in meaningful stages with persistent state, validation, and a clear recovery path.
avoidWhen: the task can fit one clear page
steps exist only for visual drama
layouts.mobile: Keep one stage per view, persist progress, place primary action in a reachable stable region.

layouts.name: Object Inspection Stage
layouts.thesis: A product object earns the visual center because rotation, hotspots, states, or configuration change understanding.
avoidWhen: a still or turntable communicates the same thing
model quality is weak
layouts.mobile: Use model-viewer or a poster-first state, limit controls, cap pixel ratio, pause offscreen.

layouts.name: Manifesto Field
layouts.thesis: Large statements and visual fields create conviction; proof interrupts at precise points rather than becoming a feature grid.
avoidWhen: the product needs detailed explanation before trust
the copy is generic
layouts.mobile: Keep the statements short, avoid viewport-height traps, place proof directly after each claim.
